correctness.rationale: For iid Pois(λ) counts, Skellam and Poisson size bias derive E min/max=λ(1∓c) and Var min/max=λ(1∓a−λc²). Thus the Fano difference equals 2(b−λc³)/(1−c²). Beta-gamma independence and strict conditional Jensen show c<(1+2λ)^(-1/2) for every λ>0. Bessel recurrences yield c′=−b/λ, b′=2c−(4+1/λ)b. If F=b−λc³ first vanished, F′=c[2−(2+4λ)c²+3λc⁴]>0 using c²<(1+2λ)^(-1), contradicting a first zero after F=λ²+O(λ³)>0 near zero. Hence universal strict positivity. Direct independent Poisson-PMF tests passed all 17 positive grid points; these do not replace the analytic proof. Asymptotic gap follows from Bessel expansions.

originality.rationale: The 2023 ultra-log-concavity theorem implies each Poisson extreme is individually underdispersed, not a mutual Fano ranking. Steutel–Thiemann (1989) supplies the exact moments, reproduced in Lederman–Schein (2025), but none of the inspectable results proves the strict relative sign at every positive intensity. Existing prior asymptotics distinguish the two ratios for sufficiently large intensities only. The nontrivial missing step is a strict cubic Bessel inequality established by a beta-gamma Jensen comparison and a global first-zero obstruction. Literature and mathematical-record searches revealed no stronger coverage; risk remains from inaccessible 1989 full text and older special-function aliases.
residual_risks: The full 1989 Eindhoven report could not be read, so an older exact-order comparison is not conclusively excluded.
Earlier equivalent modified-Bessel inequalities under special-function nomenclature could give a shorter deduction.

value.rationale: Dispersion indices quantify conditional count variability. For the smallest nontrivial Poisson order-statistic family, a globally strict rank ordering was not established by known ultra-log-concavity, exact moment, or high-intensity limit results. The theorem supplies an all-intensity comparison with a surprising opposite ordinary-variance ranking and endpoint rate; the beta-gamma convex-order route to a cubic Bessel inequality is an independent structural proof. The scope is natural and not an arbitrary parameter slice; no broader sample-size or other-parent theorem is claimed.
